newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar sees Total deal adding to '98 net.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar sees Total deal adding to '98 net.

text.p: Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp, fresh from agreeing to acquire Total Petroleum for $811 million, said Tuesday the deal will add $0.15 per share to its earnings starting in 1998.
In a telephone conference with reporters and analysts, Ultramar Chief Executive Roger Hemminghaus also said the deal will add $0.50 a share to cash flow in 1998.
"The deal will add about $0.15 to earnings and $0.50 a share to cash flow (in 1998)," Hemminghaus said.
Hemminghaus has said Wall Street analysts had estimated Ultramar Diamond would earn $2.40 to $2.50 this year.
Hemminghaus said he could not estimate how much the deal would impact 1997 earnings, but noted that most of the gains will likely be registered in 1998.
The $811 deal gives Ultramar Total's three refineries located in Colorado, Oklahoma and Michigan, as well as Total's marketing assets concentrated in the southwest and Michigan.
Ultramar, which is predicting annual savings of $50 million from the deal beginning next year, also agreed to assume $414 million of Denver-based Total Petroleum's debt.

The deal will give Total Petroleum's French parent Total SA an eight percent equity stake in the expanded Ultramar Diamond Shamrock, but that will not include a seat on Ultarmar's board, Hemminghaus said.
